chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Ben Webster: piano lessons in Kansas City, Teddy Wilson's big band, his drinking
summary: Simmons knew Ben Webster in Kansas City, discusses Teddy Wilson's big band and Ben's low tolerance for drink.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Yes. I got to know him very well. But I knew Ben in Kansas City, but I didn't know his worth at that time. See I knew him when he was taking piano lessons through a friend of my mother's and I called her Aunt Thelma but Ben studied piano in Kansas City.
What was Aunt Thelma's last name?
And Ben studied piano with her?
No, I think his piano teacher's name was Steven's if I'm not mistaken. The next time I heard of Ben he was with Teddy Wilson's big band. Did you ever hear of that band?

Oh, baby. Talk about clean. It was too clean to be a black band. That's the reason it didn't last. Because he had all of the best musicians, he sent out of state and got musicians, you know, he got Harold Baker who later was with Duke, playing first trumpet. He had a famous trombone player out of Detroit, forget his name. He had J. C. Heard on drums, Al Hall on bass. What else, that's about all I can name off hand because I didn't get to hear the band in person,
Was Ben Webster always a heavy drinker? Like he was later on.
Ben wasn't a heavy drinker, baby.
He tried to. Ben could smell a bottle and get drunk. Really.
But he used to -- well, all right, I know he got drunk, I guess I don't know how much he drank.
